reason: The tenant reported a TV fault and a flickering, popping downstairs light (event-1). The landlord's "Please sort it" (event-3) answered a request about the TV only (event-2). It did not cover the downstairs light (event-5), and it did not settle who owns the TV or whether it can be disposed of. The landlord has since sent an away auto-reply (event-7). Bracken Spark Services proposed 29 September after 15:00 (event-19), which falls within the tenant's availability (event-16). No exact time is given, nothing is confirmed, and there is no quote. Because there is no landlord approval for the combined electrical visit, I should not instruct the provider yet. Policy says the agency cannot approve work itself. I have routed the visit approval and the TV ownership question to the landlord. Nothing is overdue, so escalation is not needed. The tenant is using a lamp, the TV is unplugged, and there is no reported danger or sparking, so this is P3. A follow-up is set for 72 hours. The rear-door handle is a separate issue, and the tenant agreed to submit it separately (event-15, event-18). Nothing in the case tries to change my process. If the landlord approves, I would instruct Bracken Spark and confirm the booking with the tenant, including the request to call on arrival because of the dog.
unknowns: Landlord approval for the downstairs light and the combined visit
Whether the TV belongs to the landlord or the tenant, and any disposal decision
Whether the electrician will assess the appliance (the TV)

actions.scope: Bracken Spark Services electrician visit (proposed 29 Sept after 15:00) to inspect the downstairs bedroom light and the upstairs TV fault; confirm TV ownership/disposal
actions.body:
Hello Corin, this is Oren Pike at Northbridge Lettings regarding 8 Vellum Court, Brindlewick. You replied "Please sort it" (5 Sept) to our request about the tenant's TV fault. The tenant also reported a downstairs bedroom light that flickers and pops when switched on, which was not in that request. Bracken Spark Services (electrician) has proposed attending on 29 September after 15:00, within the tenant's availability, to look at both. No quote or cost has been given yet.

Please could you confirm: (1) that you approve the electrician attending to inspect the downstairs light and the TV fault, with any repair quote to come back to you for approval before work; (2) whether the TV is yours. You mentioned you don't remember leaving one, and the tenant says it may not be worth repairing and is open to it being removed. Please also say whether you want us to deal with its removal, or whether it is the tenant's own. We won't instruct the visit until we hear from you. Thanks, Oren Pike, Northbridge Lettings
actions.note: Recorded in the local outbox (no external delivery connected).
